title: Festival Planner
tagline: You build a spreadsheet that works the answers out for you.
objectives: Write a sum with = and box names, so the sheet works the answer out.
Change one number, say what the sums will do, and check.
Fill a sum down a column and say why its box names move.
Make a box answer in words with IF.
Pin a box with $ so a copied sum still uses it.

opening.line1: Today you make a computer do your sums for you.
opening.line2: When one number changes, it redoes every sum on its own.
opening.line3: People use spreadsheets to plan parties, trips and whole festivals.

story.b1: Hi! I am Aoife from the Lumen festival. Our planner’s laptop has stopped working.
story.b2: The money plan was on it. Tickets go on sale at 8 tonight.
story.b3: Ivy Rain is the headliner, the main act. By 8 her manager needs a yes or no. Can we afford her?

tour.s1: This grid is a sheet. Every box has a name. This one is B3: column B, row 3. Letters run along the top. Numbers run down the side.
tour.s2: This is the sum bar, also called the formula bar. Type sums here. A sum starts with = so the computer works it out.
tour.s3: Press Enter. The box then shows the answer, not the sum you typed.

sheet.locked: This box is not yours to change

c1.title: Part 1 · The grid
c1.goal: In this part you make one box do one sum. It is done when D3 shows the ticket money.
c1.show1: Watch. 1,200 tickets sell at £25 each. The * key means times.
c1.show2: Watch. Enter is pressed and D3 shows 30000. The sum has not gone. You can still see it in the Sum bar. The box itself only shows the answer.
c1.ask: Your turn. Click D3, type =B3*C3 and press Enter.
c1.h1: Click D3 first. Then type the = sign.
c1.h2: After the =, type B3, then *, then C3.
c1.h3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge.empty: D3 is still empty. Click it, type the sum, press Enter.
judge.typed: The number is right, but you typed it. Type a sum instead. Start with =, then the box names.
judge.error: The computer cannot read that sum. Check the = and the box names.
judge.wrong: That sum gives the wrong number. Multiply tickets by price: B3 * C3.
judge.no-follow: The number is right, but your sum does not use B3 and C3. Type =B3*C3. Then D3 changes whenever B3 or C3 changes.
judge.ok: D3 works out 30,000. That is £30,000 of ticket money.

c1.trick: Sorry! Tickets are 1,300, not 1,200. Can you change it?
c1.predict: Before you change B3, what will D3 show?
c1.predictRight: Yes. 1,300 times 25 is 32,500. Now change B3 and see.
c1.predictWrong: Not that one. 1,300 times 25 is 32,500. Now change B3 and see.
c1.change: Click B3, type 1300 and press Enter.

changeJudge.ok: D3 changed on its own. You never touched it.
changeJudge.no: B3 still says 1,200. Click it, type 1300, press Enter.

c1.back: Aoife again. The 1,200 tickets were right after all. Sorry! Change B3 back to 1200.

backJudge.ok: D3 is back to 30,000. Every box that uses B3 changes when B3 changes.
backJudge.no: B3 is not 1,200 yet. Click it, type 1200, press Enter.

c1.doneLine: Part 1 is done. Your sum changes when the numbers change.
c1.trick2: Here is one more change. The ticket price goes up to £30.
c1.predictRight2: Yes. 1,200 times 30 is 36,000. Now change C3 and see.
c1.predictWrong2: It will show 36,000, because 1,200 times 30 is 36,000. Now change C3 and see.

changeJudge2.ok: D3 jumped to 36,000. You changed one number and the sum did the rest.
changeJudge2.no: C3 should hold 30. Click C3, type 30, press Enter.

c1.back2: Put the price back. Click C3, type 25, press Enter.

backJudge2.ok: D3 is back to 30,000. You changed two numbers and never typed the sum again.
backJudge2.no: C3 should say 25 again. Click C3, type 25, press Enter.

c2.title: Part 2 · The copy
c2.goal: In this part you copy a sum down and add things up. It is done when D12 shows the profit. Profit is the money left after everything is paid.
c2.show1: D4 and D5 need the same sum as D3. They use the numbers one row lower.
c2.show2: Watch the little square at the bottom right of D3 being dragged down.
c2.show3: The sum is copied. D4 reads =B4*C4: the box names moved down too.
c2.ask: Drag the square on D3 down to D5. Or click D3, then Fill down.
c2.h1: Click D3. The small square sits at its bottom right corner.
c2.h2: Press and hold the left mouse button on the square. Drag down over D4 and D5. Then let go.
c2.h3: Click D3, then press Fill down. It does the drag for you.

judge.empty: D4 and D5 are still empty. Drag the square down, or press Fill down.
judge.ok: D4 shows £1,500 for car parking and D5 shows £4,800 for T-shirts. One drag made both sums.
judge.fill-wobble: D4 or D5 shows the wrong number. Click D3, then drag the square down again, or press Fill down.
judge.typed: You typed a number into D4 or D5. Click D3, then drag the square down or press Fill down.

c2.ask2: D6 is the money in. Add the three totals: type =D3+D4+D5.
c2.h2_1: Click D6. Type the = sign. Then type the three box names, with a + between each one.
c2.h2_2: The three boxes are D3, D4 and D5.
c2.h2_3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge2.typed: The number is right, but you typed it. Type a sum, so it changes when the boxes change.
judge2.error: The computer cannot read that sum. Check the = and the box names.
judge2.wrong: That gives the wrong total. Add D3, D4 and D5.
judge2.no-follow: The number is right, but the boxes are wrong. Add D3, D4 and D5.
judge2.ok: £36,300 is coming in. A shorter way is =SUM(D3:D5). It adds every box from D3 to D5.

c2.ask3: D11 is the money out. Add D8, D9 and D10 in D11, with + or SUM.
c2.h3_3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge3.typed: The number is right, but you typed it. Type a sum instead.
judge3.error: The computer cannot read that sum. Check the = and the box names.
judge3.wrong: That gives the wrong total. Add D8, D9 and D10.
judge3.no-follow: The number is right, but the boxes are wrong. Add D8, D9 and D10.
judge3.ok: The money out is £38,000. Next, work out the profit. Aoife is waiting for it.

c2.ask4: D12 is the profit: money in take away money out. Write that sum.
c2.h4_1: Profit is D6 minus D11. Minus is the - key.
c2.h4_2: Type the = sign, then D6. After that, type the - sign and then D11.
c2.h4_3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge4.typed: The number is right, but you typed it. Type a sum instead.
judge4.error: The computer cannot read that sum. Check the = and the box names.
judge4.wrong: That is not the profit. Take D11 away from D6: D6 - D11.
judge4.no-follow: The number is right, but the boxes are wrong. Use D6 and D11.
judge4.ok: D12 shows minus £1,700. The festival would lose money if it booked Ivy Rain.

c2.aoife: Minus £1,700? Oh no. Hold on, I need to think. Don’t go anywhere.
c2.doneLine: Part 2 is done. Every total changes when its numbers change.
c2.predictD6Right: Yes, the answer is 36,300. Now type the sum in D6 so that it shows 36,300.
c2.predictD6Wrong: The answer is 36,300. Now type the sum in D6 so that it shows 36,300.
c2.predictD12: Money in is 36,300. Money out is 38,000. Profit will be…
c2.predictD12Right: Yes. The money out is bigger than the money in. Write the sum in D12 and look for the minus sign.
c2.predictD12Wrong: The money out is bigger than the money in. So the profit is below zero. Write the sum in D12 and look for the minus sign.

c3.title: Part 3 · The decision
c3.goal: In this part the sheet answers a yes-or-no question by itself. It is done when D13 shows words.
c3.show1: IF is a kind of sum that asks a question. Then it picks which words to show.
c3.show2: The > sign asks: is B3 more than 1,000? Yes, so it says Big night.
c3.show3: Put three things inside the brackets, in this order. Type the question first. Next, type the words to show for yes. The words for no go last.
c3.ask: Click D13 and write an IF sum. If the profit is more than 0, it must show Book her. Otherwise it must show Not yet.
c3.h1: Type =IF( to start. Then type the question D12>0. Then type a comma.
c3.h2: Next type "Book her" in quote marks, then a comma. Then type "Not yet" in quote marks. Last, type a closing bracket.
c3.h3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge.typed: You typed the words. Use an IF sum instead, so the words change when the numbers change.
judge.error: The computer cannot read that. Check the brackets, commas and quote marks.
judge.wrong: It says Book her, but the profit is below zero. Check the order: yes words first, then no words.
judge.no-follow: The words show correctly now, but the question does not use D12, the profit. Use D12>0 as the question, so the words change when the profit changes.
judge.ok: D13 says Not yet. The sheet made its first decision. It will change when the numbers do.

c3.doneLine: Part 3 is done. The sheet can answer Aoife now. She is ringing you.
c3.test1: Wait. What if Ivy Rain’s fee were £9,000 instead of £18,000?
c3.testPredict: What will D13 say? Pick one.
c3.testRight: Yes. A cheaper fee leaves a profit above zero. Now try it.
c3.testWrong: A cheaper fee leaves a profit above zero, so D13 says Book her. Now try it.

testChangeJudge.ok: D12 is now 7,300 and D13 says Book her. You did not retype any sum.
testChangeJudge.no: D10 is not 9000 yet. Click D10, type 9000, press Enter.

c3.testBack: Sadly her fee is £18,000 after all. Click D10, type 18000, press Enter.

testBackJudge.ok: D13 says Not yet again. Your sheet now answers in words.
testBackJudge.no: D10 is not 18000 yet. Click D10, type 18000, press Enter.

c4.title: Part 4 · The call
c4.goal: In this part Aoife asks three questions on the phone. You get 90 seconds for each. It is done when she has three answers.
c4.intro: Ivy Rain’s manager is on the phone with three questions. You have 90 seconds for each question. If time runs out, Aoife asks you the same question again. The second time, there is no clock.

q.ask: If we charge £30 a ticket, do we make money?
q.predict: What do you think, before you try?
q.change: Change C3 to 30, then read D13.
q.no: Tell her: no, we lose money
q.line: At £30 the profit is £4,300, and D13 says Book her.

q.ask: Ivy Rain’s manager says only 1,000 tickets sell at £30. Do we still make money?
q.predict: What do you think, before you try?
q.change: Change B3 to 1000, then read D13.
q.yes: Tell her: yes, we still make money
q.line: The profit is minus £1,700 again. 1,000 tickets at £30 earn the same as 1,200 at £25.

q.ask: Last one. If 1,100 tickets sell at £32, do we make money?
q.predict: What do you think, before you try?
q.change: Change B3 to 1100 and C3 to 32, then read D13.
q.line: The profit is £3,500, so D13 says Book her. Aoife is cheering down the phone.

c4.predictedRight: Your guess was right. The sheet agrees.
c4.predictedWrong: The sheet shows something different from your guess. Checking was a good idea.
c4.notYet: D13 does not show the answer yet. Make the change that the question asks for. Then read D13 again.
c4.wrongAnswer: Read D13 again. Your answer does not match it.
c4.timeout: Time ran out and the call ended. Aoife rings back with the same question. There is no clock this time.
c4.hintsOpen: You can ask for hints now. Press Give me a hint if you need one.
c4.doneLine: Part 4 is done. Aoife has her three answers.

c5.title: Part 5 · The pin
c5.goal: In this part you add VAT, a tax, to the shop prices. It is done when one box changes every price.
c5.intro1: Click the Shop tab. It holds what we sell. VAT is a tax added to every price.
c5.intro2: The VAT rate is in B1. Today it is 0.2, which means 20%. It can change later.
c5.show1: To add VAT, multiply the price by (1 + rate). The rate is 0.2, so that is times 1.2. For the T-shirt, type =B3*(1+B1).
c5.ask: Click C3 and type the T-shirt sum: =B3*(1+B1). Press Enter.
c5.h1: Click C3, then type = and B3.
c5.h2: Then type *, then (1+B1) with the brackets.
c5.h3: Type exactly this, then press Enter:

judge.typed: The number is right, but you typed it. Type a sum instead.
judge.error: The computer cannot read that. Check the brackets.
judge.wrong: That is not £14.40. Multiply the price by (1 + rate): B3*(1+B1).
judge.no-follow: The number is right, but the boxes are wrong. Use B3 and B1.
judge.ok: C3 shows £14.40 for a T-shirt. Now fill it down to C6 for the other items.

c5.wobble: Look at C4, C5 and C6. Something has gone wrong.
c5.wobbleWhy1: Click C4. Its sum reads =B4*(1+B2). The copy moved B1 down to B2.
c5.wobbleWhy2: But B2 is the word Price, not the rate. The rate must not move.
c5.pin1: Pin the rate box so copies cannot move it. Write it as $B$1. The two $ signs are the pin.
c5.pin2: A pinned box stays put when the sum is copied.
c5.knew: You already pinned B1. Here is why it matters:
c5.ask3: Click C3, type =B3*(1+$B$1), press Enter. Then fill down to C6.
c5.h3_1: To type a $ sign, hold down Shift and press 4.
c5.h3_2: Put $ before the B and $ before the 1: $B$1.
c5.h3_3: Type exactly this, press Enter, then Fill down:

judge3.typed: You typed a number into one of the prices. Click C3, then fill down, so all four prices are sums.
judge3.error: The computer cannot read that. Check the brackets and the $ signs.
judge3.wrong: C3 is not £14.40. Check the brackets.
judge3.no-follow: The number is right, but C3 does not use both B3 and $B$1. Use B3 and $B$1, with both $ signs.
judge3.fill-wobble: One of the rows below C3 is still wrong. Click C3 and check it says $B$1 with both $ signs. Then press Fill down again.
judge3.ok: The four prices are 14.40, 36.00, 9.60 and 6.00. All four use the one pinned box.

c5.whatif: VAT might go up to 25% next year. What would the hoodie cost?
c5.predict: Before you change B1, what will C4 show?
c5.predictRight: Yes. The hoodie costs £30. With VAT at 25%, you multiply by 1.25, and 30 times 1.25 is 37.50. Now change B1 and see.
c5.predictWrong: Not that one. The hoodie costs £30. With VAT at 25%, you multiply by 1.25, and 30 times 1.25 is 37.50. Now change B1 and see.
c5.change: Click B1, type 0.25 and press Enter.

changeJudge.ok: Every price changed. One pinned box controls all of them.
changeJudge.no: B1 is not 0.25 yet. Click it, type 0.25, press Enter.

c5.doneLine: Part 5 is done. You can pin a box with $ signs, and you know why it matters.
c5.predict2: Next you will change the hoodie price in B4 to £40. Before you do, which boxes in column C will change?
c5.predict2Right: Yes, only C4 changes. Each row uses its own price and the one pinned rate in B1.
c5.predict2Wrong: Not that one. Only C4 changes. Each row uses its own price and the one pinned rate in B1.

change2Judge.ok: C4 now shows 50.00. You changed one price, so only C4 changed.
change2Judge.no: B4 is not 40 yet. Click B4, type 40, press Enter.

poster.title: Your poster
poster.intro: Here is the night you made possible.
poster.sub: One night of lanterns and music by the lough
poster.rename: Rename the festival if you like

badges.name: The Copy
badges.line: You copied a sum down. The box names in it moved down too.

free.text: Find the lowest whole-pound ticket price that still books Ivy Rain. On the Plan tab, try prices in C3.
free.ok: You found it. At £27 a ticket you book her, and £700 is left over.
free.over: At £{v} the sheet says Book her. Can a lower price still book her?
free.under: At £{v} the sheet does not say Book her yet. Try a price one pound higher.
free.reset: For this challenge, leave the tickets at 1,200 and the fee at £18,000.

free.text: Put the price back to £25. Now find the fewest tickets that still book her. Try numbers in B3.
free.ok: You found it. 1,269 tickets at £25 each book her.
free.over: With {v} tickets the sheet says Book her. Can fewer tickets still book her?
free.under: With {v} tickets the sheet does not say Book her yet. Try more tickets.
free.reset: For this challenge, leave the price at £25 and the fee at £18,000.

free.text: You choose. Change any numbers, but keep D13 saying Book her. Then tell your teacher your plan.
